title: All-Edges Triangle in the (n, n, sqrt n) tripartite regime
credit: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, 'Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs', arXiv:2610.06783 (2026)
premise_risks: arXiv:2610.06783 (Alman-Vassilevska Williams, Oct 2026, unrefereed): source of the regime, of the refutation of the APSP-type hardness at this boundary, and of the m^{4/3} balanced-hardness framing.
arXiv:2610.17420 (Majdoddin, Oct 2026, unrefereed): extension of thin products to middle part D <= N^{0.172}, cited as the best partial progress.
plain: Given a tripartite graph with parts of sizes n, n, sqrt(n) and O(n^{3/2}) edges, determine for every edge whether it lies in a triangle in O(n^{2-eps}) time (combinatorial or algebraic).
math: Is there ε > 0 and a randomized word-RAM algorithm that, for every tripartite graph on A, B, C with |A| = |B| = n, |C| = ceil(sqrt n) and O(n^{3/2}) edges, decides for every edge whether it lies in a triangle in time O(n^{2-ε})? (Main question; a fine-grained reduction from balanced All-Edges Sparse Triangle at m^{4/3-o(1)} would be evidence for a negative answer but is not itself a disproof.)
lean_gap: Not formalized: needs a word-RAM model with time accounting, randomized algorithms, and fine-grained reductions, none of which Mathlib provides.
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
